passage.title: 'The Causeway', teacher-written modern memoir for TGA
paras: They tell you the tide comes in slowly. It does not. One moment the sand bar was a wide, rippled road between the island and the shore; the next, a thin silver line had appeared on either side of it, and the silver was moving. We walked faster. Then we ran. My little sister held my sleeve so tightly that the next day there were four small bruises on my arm, one for each finger. We reached the causeway steps with our shoes full of sea. Behind us the road had gone, as if it had never been there at all.

blocks.h: Three common gaps and their fixes

head: Gap
Fix
rows: Q7 one text at a time

model.title: How does the writer use language and structure to present the danger?

parts.text: Opening: a calm claim overturned: 'It does not.'
Language: the tide as 'a thin silver line' that is 'moving'
Structure: sentences shorten as the danger grows
Ending: 'as if it had never been there at all' (the road erased)

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The writer overturns the reader's calm at once ('It does not.'), then makes the threat beautiful and quiet, 'a thin silver line', until short sentences ('Then we ran.') quicken the pace; the ending erases the road 'as if it had never been there at all', so the danger seems almost unreal.

questions.q: Write your weakest reading question and the habit you will fix
Zoom into 'four small bruises' and explain the effect
questions.a: The precise, physical detail shows how frightened the sister was, and the danger's lasting mark.

questions.q: Core (timed, 12 minutes): in the portal response box, answer 'How does the writer use language and structure to present the danger?' (10 marks), applying your fix
questions.a: Mark scheme points: calm claim overturned; 'thin silver line' (beauty and threat); shortening sentences; the sister's grip and 'four small bruises'; 'shoes full of sea'; ending erasing the road.

questions.q: Extend: self-mark with the ladder and compare with your Paper 2 level
Stretch: write one Q7-style sentence comparing 'The Causeway' with 'The Night the River Came In'
questions.a: For example: 'Both writers show water arriving with frightening speed, but the causeway memoir is about one family's escape, whereas the flood memoir is about a street pulling together.'

questions.q: Which sentence would earn most in Q3?
options: The short sentences 'We walked faster. Then we ran.' quicken the pace, so the reader feels the panic rise.
The tide comes in and they run.
questions.a: A) The short sentences 'We walked faster. Then we ran.' quicken the pace, so the reader feels the panic rise.. Method, quotation and effect together.
